title: Reconstruct a disputed expedition chronology
objective: Recover all supported event orders from letters with relative dates and a reused vessel name.
semantic_rule: Only explicit relative dates within the same voyage support edges; retain unresolved voyage identity.
output_contract:
{ "V1_order": (string)[]; "V2_edges": ((string)[])[]; "unassigned": (string)[] }
Output representation: V1_order is an ordered sequence of source-grounded event descriptions; clear equivalent event names are allowed, and underscores versus spaces do not change event identity. V2_edges contains ordered earlier/later event-description pairs. The unassigned list contains record IDs: in this task record-NN.txt has ID rN, where N is its decimal file number without leading zeros. Preserve the voyage distinction even when event descriptions coincide.
positive_evidence: Voyage V1 aboard Lark begins with departure on day 1.
The V1 ice landing occurs three days after departure.
negative_evidence: V1 departure and V2 departure are different events; calendar day numbers use the same supplied calendar.

records.text: Voyage V1 aboard Lark begins with departure on day 1.
The V1 ice landing occurs three days after departure.
V1 engineer: engine repair begins after the ice landing.
V1 captain: return occurs on day 20, after engine repair.
V1 supplies were loaded before departure.
V1 customs inspection happened after loading and before departure.
V1 sounding survey followed the ice landing but preceded engine repair.
V1 anchor test followed engine repair.
V1 north camp was established after the anchor test.
V1 specimen collection took place after north camp was established.
V1 weather watch began after specimen collection.
V1 south camp was established after the weather watch.
V1 ice crossing occurred after south camp was established.
V1 mast inspection followed the ice crossing.
V1 mast repair followed the mast inspection.
V1 radio test followed mast repair.
V1 final inventory followed the radio test.
V1 harbor approach followed final inventory and preceded return.
V2 also used a cutter named Lark, but has its own voyage identifier.
V2 departure was day 100; its repair occurred before that departure.
An undated scrap says Lark repaired before departure; no voyage is named.
V1 clerk uses sounding survey and depth survey as aliases for the same event.
V1 witness says depth survey preceded engine repair, confirming the engineer sequence.
V1 departure and V2 departure are different events; calendar day numbers use the same supplied calendar.

title: Date deposits with residual and intrusive finds

Scout S carries a relic and proposes two-space movement; knight K is not a scout.
Puzzle proof requires noticing mirror writing, reversing STAR, and entering RATS.
Hint level1 may reveal orientation matters; level2 may name reversal; level3 may give the final answer.
Player requests hint level1 and has not noticed the mirror.
Treasure initially lies in cave; guard G knows that initial location.
Treasure moves to tower while G is absent; thief T witnesses the move.
T tells G it remains in cave; G believes T, with no later observation.
Agent search decisions use each agent own belief, not narrator world knowledge.
Cooperative player Ada can hold switch SW; Bo can cross bridge BR only while SW is held.
Bo can retrieve key CK beyond BR and return; Ada then uses CK to open gate CG.
No one can wedge SW, and starting inventory has no CK.
Ada must keep holding SW while Bo crosses in either direction.
Rule trade: spend one token to gain one gem.
Rule refund: discard one gem to gain two tokens.
The audited cycle consists of at most one trade and one refund, starting with one token and zero gems.
Balance invariant says completing that trade-refund cycle must not increase tokens.
Complete a finite legal sequence; an exploit witness must obey each operation precondition.
Any movement exception applies only to its named unit category and carried item state.
A story mention of a key does not place that key in inventory.
A character statement can alter another character belief without altering the world state.
A hint is judged by information disclosed, not merely by omitting the exact final token.
Plans and counterexamples are returned as data; the simulated game is not mutated.

3. Add four cross-folder references to those new items, with at least two aliases whose equivalence is stated in a separate source record.
4. Instantiate this exact causal intervention as a separate revision branch: Player requests level 3; the final answer may be disclosed.
5. Add at least four evidence records tracing how that intervention changes downstream decisions; include one unchanged neighboring result and explain why it remains unchanged.

Puzzle proof requires noticing mirror writing, reversing STAR, and entering RATS.
Hint level1 may reveal orientation matters; level2 may name reversal; level3 may give the final answer.
Player requests hint level1 and has not noticed the mirror.
Treasure initially lies in cave; guard G knows that initial location.
Treasure moves to tower while G is absent; thief T witnesses the move.
T tells G it remains in cave; G believes T, with no later observation.
Agent search decisions use each agent own belief, not narrator world knowledge.
Cooperative player Ada can hold switch SW; Bo can cross bridge BR only while SW is held.
Bo can retrieve key CK beyond BR and return; Ada then uses CK to open gate CG.
No one can wedge SW, and starting inventory has no CK.
Ada must keep holding SW while Bo crosses in either direction.
Rule trade: spend one token to gain one gem.
Rule refund: discard one gem to gain two tokens.
The audited cycle consists of at most one trade and one refund, starting with one token and zero gems.
Balance invariant says completing that trade-refund cycle must not increase tokens.
Complete a finite legal sequence; an exploit witness must obey each operation precondition.
Any movement exception applies only to its named unit category and carried item state.
A story mention of a key does not place that key in inventory.
A character statement can alter another character belief without altering the world state.
A hint is judged by information disclosed, not merely by omitting the exact final token.
Plans and counterexamples are returned as data; the simulated game is not mutated.
